What's here
-----------
  - *.js         package/dist/*.js verbatim (swc-compiled ESM, relative
                 imports only — loads as-is under the no-build rule)
  - *.d.ts       package/typings/*.d.ts verbatim, renamed to SIBLINGS of
                 the .js files so tsc resolves each import to real types
                 (dev-only; never loaded at runtime)
  - VERSION      the pinned npm release the bytes came from
  - LICENSE-MIT / LICENSE-APACHE  upstream license texts
  (dist/tsconfig.tsbuildinfo is build residue — not vendored)

What it is
----------
A small (~40 KB, dependency-free) TypeScript implementation of the WASI
preview1 syscall surface for browsers: fd_read/fd_write, an in-memory
File/Directory tree behind path_open, args/env/clock — enough to run a
wasm32-wasi binary against a virtual filesystem. peerd wraps it in the
`peerd:wasi` Notebook builtin (notebook-tab/notebook-wasi.js) to run
WASI modules inside the sealed worker.

Audit notes (reviewed 2026-07-06, v0.4.2)
-----------------------------------------
  - ZERO network or dynamic-code primitives: no fetch / XMLHttpRequest /
    WebSocket / eval / new Function / importScripts / postMessage /
    navigator anywhere in the dist. The shim is pure syscall emulation
    over caller-supplied Fd objects — every capability a module gets is
    an object the CALLER constructed and passed in. That deny-by-default
    shape is why this library and not a batteries-included runtime.
  - fs_opfs.js (SyncOPFSFile) touches OPFS sync access handles only if
    the caller hands it one; peerd's wrapper never does (in-memory File
    trees only). Kept verbatim because index.js re-exports it.
  - No workers spawned, no SharedArrayBuffer required, no wasm bytes of
    its own — the only WebAssembly interaction is reading the module's
    exported memory.
  - GOTCHA: the WASI constructor calls debug.enable(options.debug)
    unconditionally, and enable(undefined) means enable(TRUE) — omit the
    options bag and every syscall logs a "wasi:" console line. Callers
    must pass { debug: false } (notebook-wasi.js does).

Update procedure
----------------
1. Bump WASI_SHIM_VERSION + EXPECTED_TARBALL_SHA256 in
   scripts/vendor-wasi-shim.sh (verify the new tarball hash out of band).
2. Run the script; it re-pulls, verifies, and rewrites the files here.
3. Re-audit the diff against the notes above (grep for the network/eval
   primitives), re-record the SHA-256s and date in this file.
